answer: Voting weight here follows a convex function of stake and tenure, so one walnut account with long tenure counts for more than the sum of its clones. Forking that stake across a fresh summit of new identities drops each fragment below the convex curve, discarding weight with every split. An attacker must weave a fresh thread of months-long tenure separately for each new identity, since convexity cannot be restored by recombining split stakes, so cost per extra identity keeps climbing.
